slides.prompt: How did Covid-19 change the world?
slides.hint: Monday we used 4 checks to find a missing link.
slides.notes: 60-min Tue lesson, sl_t1. Opening hook for Module p.69. Monday one-liner only, no reteaching. Outcomes (teacher-kept): read the passage clearly for PBD; use 6 new words in own sentences.

slides.prompt: Before we open the book — what changed?
items: Life was disrupted, but people cooperated.
Hygiene and technology keep us connected.
slides.notes: Prime the passage ideas in its own vocabulary. Partner talk 1 min: which change still helps us today? Point and say why.
Elicit first, then reveal. Word 1 of 6.

slides.feedback: Vaccines reduced the severity of illness.
slides.notes: Word 2 of 6. Sets up the weak-vs-strong slide.
Word 3 of 6. -let spotlight per SOT: drop + -let, book + -let, leaf + -let.
Word 6 of 6. Module gloss follows p.69. Misconception: pupils copy definitions — enforce show, don't repeat.

columns.label: B
columns.text: Vaccines reduced the severity of illness so fewer people became very sick.

slides.hint: Look for an action and a result.
slides.notes: Frame: word + action + detail + because/so + result. Copy the habit, not the sentence.

slides.prompt: PBD round: read clearly, use the word.
items: Teacher picks names with the randomizer.
Use one word in your own sentence.
slides.notes: Teacher goes around testing against LS 3.1.5 (read the article) and LS 3.1.4 (word meanings); about 8 readers. Passage stays in the book (copyright). No names in artifacts.

slides.task: Choose one word: resilient, severity, droplet, vital, disruption or significant. Write one strong sentence about your life or school that shows its meaning.
slides.frame: Word + action + detail + because / so + result.
slides.notes: 5 min silent exit. Bridge: Thursday turns the p.70 handwashing essay into an information-transfer table. Collect short/long books after.
